REMARKS

Applicant has carefully reviewed the non-final Office Action mailed on December 2, 2024, and offers the following remarks to accompany the above amendments. Further, the Applicant would like to request an Examiner interview to discuss any unresolved issues.
Examiner Interview
Applicant wishes to thank Examiner Hodge and Primary Examiner Jian for the telephonic interview conducted on December 23, 2024. Examiner Hodge indicated that specifying the placement of the sensors should advance the prosecution under the currently pending 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection.
Summary of Remarks
Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 17, and 21 to indicate approximate anterior positions of a first acoustic sensor and an optical sensor relative to a maternal torso.
Status of the Claims
Claims 1, 4-5, 7-9, 11, 13-14, 17, 19-21, 23, and 25 were previously pending. Claims 2-3, 6, 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, and 24 were previously canceled. Claims 1, 4-5, 7-9, 13-14, 16- 17, 19-21, and 23 are amended herein. Claims 11 and 25 are canceled herein. New claims 26-29 are added herein. As such, claims 1, 4-5, 7-9, 11, 13-14, 17, 19-21, 23, and 26-29 remain pending.

Objection to the Claims

Claim 21 is objected to due to a spelling error. The cited limitation of claim 21 has been amended as follows:

Claim Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 101

Claims 1, 4-5, 7-9, 11, 13-14, 16-17, 19-21, 23, and 25 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed invention is directed to a judicial exception, specifically an abstract idea without significantly more.
Claim 1 has been amended to recite:
(Currently Amended) A fetal monitoring patch wearable fetal health monitoring device for determining a health condition of a fetus based on biosignals of an expecting mother and the fetus, the fetal monitoring patch
wearable fetal health monitoring device comprising:
[[an]] a first acoustic sensor configured to provide mechano- acoustically sensed phonocardiogram (aPCG) data from afirst an anterior
side location on a maternal torso;
an optical sensor configured to provide optically sensed maternal
photoplethysmogram (mPPG) data from a second an anterior centralized location on the maternal torso relative to the anterior side location, wherein
the first location and the second location are mutually exclusive;
a breathable substrate securing device configured toprovide skin
contact of the frst acoustic sensor via a first acoustic impedance coupler

non-invasive non-clinical monitoring; and
a microcontroller mechanically coupled with the breathable substrate,
wherein the microcontroller is configured for:
continuously monitoring fetal movement (fM) using the frst acoustic sensor
while operating in a first mode, wherein the first mode is a low-power
vigilant monitoring state; and
upon detecting reducedfM activity, transitioning to a second mode comprising: decomposing the mechano-acoustically sensed aPCG data using the optically
sensed mPPG    data to extract mechano-acoustically sensed fetal
phonocardiogram (fPCG) data;
determining fetal heart rate variability (fHRV) data from the mechano- acoustically sensed fPCG data; and
providing an alert to the expecting mother based on the fHR V data, wherein the
alert is indicative of a medical emergency.

[0051] A simplified component layout of a wearable fetal
monitoring device in the form of a wearable pressure adhesive patch 110 (alternately referred to herein as "patch 110" or "patch') is shown in FIGS. 3A, SB and C. FIG. 3A illustrates a nondermal distal side ofpatch 110 with primaly components visible. In one embodiment, components of
908/17 UTIL
Page 14 of 21


patch 110 are placed on a flexible board and connected with one or more flexible interconnects 309. The components of patch 110 can comprise a microcontroller 301. In one embodiment, microcontroller 301 can comprise one of one or multiple cores capable of ultralow power sleep states. The components of patch 110 can further comprise a wireless communication module 302. In one embodiment, wireless communication module 302 can comprise one or more of the following sub-components: chip antenna, rigid-island antenna, flexible antenna, and similar other sub-components.
The components of patch 110 cab furthermore comprise a memory data storage 303. In one embodiment, memory data storage 303 can comprise a non-volatile memory data storage such as, for example, a Quad-SPI non- volatile memory data storage. The components of patch 110 can additionally comprise power management circuit 304 and a power source 305. In one embodiment, patch 110 includes a breathable substrate 310.
In one embodiment, a biocompatible material engineered to match the acoustic impedance of soft tissue is shown in the dermal contact side of patch 110. In one embodiment, patch 110 further includes an acoustic impedance coupler 308. In one embodiment, acoustic impedance coupler 308 is the primary point ofskin contactfor acoustic sensors 306 to minimize reflected signal loss due to acoustic impedance mismatch between the fetal health monitoring device and soft tissue. Since fetal signal is generally low magnitude, maximizing signal transmission to transducer is key for accurate feature extraction. The material in acoustic impedance coupler 308 can be composed of polydimethylsiloxane adjusted with TiO2 nanoparticles. In another embodiment, material of acoustic impedance coupler 308 can be composed of modified polyurethane or other
nanocomposites.

Amended claim 1 is directed toward a specific structure (i.e. afetal monitoring patch) including a specific materal (i.e. a breathable substrate) and approximate anterior positions of afirst acoustic sensor and an optical sensor relative to a maternal torso. Clearly the fetal monitor patch of amended claim 1 is much more than an abstract idea. As such amended claim 1 is allowable.
Claims 4-5, 7-9, 13-14, 16, and 23 depend directly from amended claim 1 and are allowable at least by virtue of their dependence from amended claim 1.
Claims 17 and 21 have been amended to include features similar to now allowable claim 1. As such claims 17 and 21 are also allowable.
Claims 19-20 depend directly from amended claim 17 and are allowable at least by virtue of their dependence from amended claim 17.
Claims 11 and 25 have been canceled rendering their rejection moot.
Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 of claims 1, 4-5, 7-9, 13-14, 17, 19-21, and 23 be withdrawn.
